blocks.text: **Human rights** are the inherent, universal rights of all persons, protected in India through the **Constitution (Fundamental Rights), the Protection of Human Rights Act (1993), and the NHRC/SHRCs**, and globally through the **UDHR and UN mechanisms**.

rows: **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR, 1948)**; ICCPR & ICESCR covenants.
**Fundamental Rights (Part III)**; **Protection of Human Rights Act (1993)**.
Statutory; chaired by a former **CJI or SC judge**; recommendatory powers; investigates violations.
**Custodial violence, recommendatory (not binding) powers, delays, armed-forces exemption**.

items: UDHR (1948); NHRC (1993, statutory) — recommendatory powers only; headed by ex-CJI/SC judge.
Protection of Human Rights Act 1993 = the enabling law.

prelimsPointers: **UDHR** adopted by the UN on **10 Dec 1948** (Human Rights Day).
Two covenants — **ICCPR (civil-political) & ICESCR (economic-social-cultural)**.
**Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993** created the **NHRC & SHRCs**.
**NHRC** — chaired by a former **Chief Justice/Judge of the Supreme Court**; **recommendatory** powers.
NHRC's recommendations are **not binding**; a key limitation.
**Human Rights Day — 10 December**.
India is a party to major UN human-rights conventions.
mainsAngles: Assess the role and limitations of the NHRC in protecting human rights.

glossary.definition: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), the foundational global human-rights document.
The National Human Rights Commission, a statutory body (1993) with recommendatory powers.
The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, a binding UN human-rights treaty.

blocks.text: Women's rights in India are protected by **constitutional guarantees, a body of protective legislation, and institutions like the National Commission for Women** — reinforced by **reservation in local bodies** and recent measures against violence and for empowerment.

rows: **Equality (14-15), no discrimination, Art. 15(3) special provisions, Art. 39(d) equal pay, 42 maternity relief, 243D/T (⅓ reservation in local bodies)**.
**Dowry Prohibition (1961), PCPNDT (1994), Domestic Violence Act (2005), Sexual Harassment at Workplace/POSH (2013), Maternity Benefit (Amend. 2017)**.
**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Amendment, 2023)** — ⅓ seats in Lok Sabha & assemblies (on delimitation).
**Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PM Matru Vandana, Ujjwala, One Stop Centres**.

items: 106th Amendment (2023, Nari Shakti Vandan) = ⅓ women's reservation in Lok Sabha/assemblies.
Key laws: Domestic Violence 2005, POSH 2013, PCPNDT; NCW 1992.

prelimsPointers: **Article 15(3)** allows the state to make **special provisions for women & children**.
**106th Amendment (2023) — Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam** — reserves **⅓ seats** for women in the Lok Sabha & state assemblies.
**National Commission for Women (NCW)** — statutory body, **1992**.
**Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**; **POSH Act, 2013** (Vishaka guidelines).
**PCPNDT Act (1994)** — bans sex-selective abortion; **Dowry Prohibition Act (1961)**.
**Sabarimala, triple talaq (2019 Act)** — recent gender-justice developments.
Schemes — **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, PM Matru Vandana Yojana, Ujjwala, One Stop Centres**.
mainsAngles: Discuss the constitutional and legislative framework for women's empowerment in India.

glossary.definition: The 106th Amendment (2023) reserving one-third of legislative seats for women.
The National Commission for Women, a statutory body (1992) safeguarding women's rights.
The 2013 law against sexual harassment of women at the workplace.

blocks.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes enjoy a comprehensive framework of **constitutional safeguards — social, economic, political, educational and service** — plus special protective laws and national commissions, aimed at ending historic discrimination and ensuring social justice.

rows: **Reservation of seats (Arts. 330, 332)** in Lok Sabha & assemblies; local bodies.
**Fifth & Sixth Schedules, PESA (1996), Forest Rights Act (2006)**.

items: Art 17 (untouchability), 330/332 (seat reservation), PoA Act 1989, FRA 2006, PESA 1996.
NCSC (338), NCST (338A) constitutional; 5th/6th Schedules for tribal areas.

prelimsPointers: **Article 17** — abolishes **untouchability**; **Art. 15(2)** bans discrimination in public places.
**Reservation of seats — Articles 330 (Lok Sabha) & 332 (Assemblies)** for SC/ST.
**SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989** — against caste atrocities.
**NCSC (Article 338), NCST (Article 338A), NCBC (Article 338B)**.
**Fifth Schedule** (mainland tribal areas) & **Sixth Schedule** (NE autonomous districts).
**PESA (1996)** & **Forest Rights Act (2006)** empower tribal communities.
**Article 335** — SC/ST claims in services consistent with efficiency of administration.
mainsAngles: Examine the constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

glossary.definition: The SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, penalising caste-based atrocities.
The 2006 law recognising forest-dwelling tribes' rights over land and forest produce.
The constitutional provision for autonomous tribal district councils in the North-East.

blocks.text: **Child rights** in India are protected by **constitutional provisions, a set of dedicated laws (POCSO, RTE, Juvenile Justice, child-labour ban), and the NCPCR** — aligned with the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**.

rows: **RTE Act (2009), POCSO (2012), Juvenile Justice Act (2015), Child Labour (Prohibition) Act, Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (2006)**.
Statutory body protecting child rights; monitors RTE/POCSO.
**UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC, 1989)** — India ratified 1992.

items: Art 21A (RTE), 24 (child labour); POCSO 2012, RTE 2009, JJ Act 2015; NCPCR 2007.

prelimsPointers: **Article 21A** — Right to Education (6-14) via the **86th Amendment (2002)**; **RTE Act (2009)**.
**Article 24** — prohibits child labour below 14 in hazardous work.
**POCSO Act (2012)** — protection of children from sexual offences.
**Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection) Act, 2015**; **Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006**.
**NCPCR (2007)** — statutory child-rights commission.
**UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989)** — India ratified in **1992**.
Schemes — **ICDS/Anganwadi, Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**.
mainsAngles: Discuss the legal framework for the protection of child rights in India.

glossary.definition: The 2012 law protecting children from sexual offences.
The Right to Education Act (2009) implementing Article 21A for children aged 6-14.
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights, a statutory body (2007).

blocks.text: Government delivers development and welfare through a wide array of **flagship central schemes and state (AP) programmes** spanning **financial inclusion, health, housing, employment, sanitation and direct benefit transfers** — a high-yield current-affairs area.

rows: **Jan Dhan Yojana, DBT, Mudra, Stand-Up India**.
**Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY), National Health Mission, Mission Indradhanush**.
**PM Awas Yojana, Swachh Bharat, Jal Jeevan Mission**.
**Rythu Bharosa, Amma Vodi, YSR/NTR welfare schemes, AP Fibre Grid**.

items: Map schemes to domains (Jan Dhan-finance, Ayushman-health, PMAY-housing, MGNREGA-employment).
AP schemes (Rythu Bharosa, Amma Vodi) add state-specific value.

prelimsPointers: **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (2014)** — financial inclusion (zero-balance accounts).
**Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY)** — world's largest health-assurance scheme (₹5 lakh cover).
**PM Awas Yojana** (housing), **Swachh Bharat** (sanitation), **Jal Jeevan Mission** (tap water).
**MGNREGA** — 100 days' guaranteed wage employment; **PM-KISAN** — ₹6000/yr to farmers.
**Mudra, Stand-Up India, Start-Up India** — enterprise/credit.
**DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer)** uses the **JAM trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile)**.
AP schemes — **Rythu Bharosa (farmers), Amma Vodi (education), YSR/NTR welfare, AP Fibre Grid**.
mainsAngles: Assess the impact of flagship welfare schemes on inclusive development.

glossary.definition: Direct Benefit Transfer — routing subsidies straight to beneficiaries' bank accounts.
The Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile combination enabling targeted benefit delivery.
The national health-assurance scheme (PM-JAY) offering ₹5 lakh hospitalisation cover.
